info.name: EDK Enterprise REST
info.description:
Common developer journeys against an EDK Enterprise deployment.

1. **Platform operator**: list the tenants or register one.
2. **Tenant owner**: create a service client for your applications (or do it in the admin console).
3. **Tenant APIs**: everything else, with the service client's OAuth2 token: keys and DIDs, Azure Key Vault, issuing and verifying credentials, status lists, trust domains and a Keycloak wallet login.

Set two values in the environment: `baseDomain` (for example `example.com`) and `tenantSlug` (for example `acme`). The platform is at `https://platform.<baseDomain>` and the tenant at `https://<tenantSlug>.<baseDomain>`; every URL follows from these two. Each folder sets up its own OAuth2 token: open the folder's **Authorization** tab and choose **Get New Access Token**.

Ids that a request needs are captured from earlier list or create responses, so start a folder at its first request. Folders marked optional need extra inputs and skip their requests until you set them.

Documentation: https://docs.sphereon.com/edk/deployment/onboarding-walkthrough

exec: // All URLs are built from two environment values: baseDomain and tenantSlug.
// The platform lives at platform.<baseDomain>, a tenant at <tenantSlug>.<baseDomain>.
throw new Error('Set baseDomain in your environment to a bare domain such as example.com (add :port only if your gateway uses one).');

item.name: 1. Platform operator
item.description:
Requests on `platform.<baseDomain>` that only the platform operator may make.

**Sign in:** open this folder, go to **Authorization** and choose **Get New Access Token**. Sign in with the platform operator account in the window that opens, then choose **Use Token**.

Documentation: https://docs.sphereon.com/edk/deployment/onboarding-walkthrough

item.name: 2. Tenant owner: create a service client
item.description:
Your applications call the tenant APIs with a **service client**: an OAuth2 client of the tenant's own authorization server that uses the client-credentials grant, with no user involved. Create it here once as the tenant owner, or in the admin console under **Authorization server > Clients**. Either way, put its id and secret in `serviceClientId` and `serviceClientSecret`.

**Sign in:** open this folder, go to **Authorization** and choose **Get New Access Token**. Sign in as the tenant owner (the account you activated with the owner link), then choose **Use Token**.

Documentation: https://docs.sphereon.com/edk/guides/journeys/platform-foundations/authorization-server

request.description: Creates a confidential client with the client-credentials grant and the `tenant-admin` role. `allowedAccessTokenAudiences` names the tenant services its tokens may call. The secret is set by you and never returned: when `serviceClientSecret` is empty, a random one is generated and stored in your environment.
Secrets cannot be read back. Send this when you lost the secret of an existing client: it stores `serviceClientSecret` (generated when empty) as the new secret.

item.name: 3. Tenant APIs
item.description:
Everything your applications do on `<tenantSlug>.<baseDomain>`, with the service client's token.

**Get a token:** set `serviceClientId` and `serviceClientSecret` (folder 2 fills in the secret when it creates the client). Open this folder, go to **Authorization**, choose **Get New Access Token**, then **Use Token**. Postman asks for one token that is valid for all tenant services; get a new one when it expires after an hour.

Each folder starts by listing what exists, and stores the ids that later requests use.

const mod = (v, m) => { const r = v % m; return r >= 0n ? r : r + m; };
const inv = (v, m) => { let [a, b, x, y] = [mod(v, m), m, 1n, 0n]; while (a > 1n) { const q = b / a; [a, b] = [b - q * a, a]; [x, y] = [y - q * x, x]; } return mod(x, m); };

item.name: Set up the wallet proxy
item.description:
A second authorization server, the **wallet proxy**, is hosted at `/as/<walletProxySlug>` and sends wallet users to Keycloak to sign in. The tenant's default authorization server is not changed, and no credential uses the proxy until you choose so in the next folder.

In Keycloak, create a confidential OpenID Connect client with the standard flow and this redirect URI: `https://<tenantSlug>.<baseDomain>/as/wallet-proxy/federation/callback`. Set `keycloakIssuer` (for example `https://idp.example.com/realms/acme`), `keycloakClientId` and `keycloakClientSecret`. Keycloak needs no OID4VCI support. Each step checks what exists first, so you can run the folder again. Documentation: https://docs.sphereon.com/edk/guides/tenant/federation

item.name: 6. Wallet: request the credential
item.description: Open this folder's **Authorization** tab and choose **Get New Access Token**. The authorization request carries `issuer_state` and `authorization_details`; sign in at Keycloak, then choose **Use Token**.
